amillennial: Christ is reigning now from heaven; the "thousand years" symbolizes the whole church age.
cessationist: Miraculous gifts like tongues and prophecy ended with the apostles; God doesn't give them today.
complementarian: God designed men and women for distinct, complementary roles — including male leadership in church and home.
congregational: Each local church governs itself, answering to no higher authority.
continuationist: Miraculous gifts like tongues and prophecy are still given to the church today.
covenant theology: God has one unfolding plan of salvation through covenants, centered on Christ from Genesis to Revelation.
credobaptism: Baptism is for people old enough to profess faith in Christ themselves — "believer's baptism."
dispensational: God works through distinct eras and keeps separate plans for Israel and the church.
egalitarian: Men and women may serve equally in every role, in church and home — gifting matters, not gender.
entire sanctification: Christians can experience a definite work of grace that breaks sin's control in this life.
free grace: Salvation comes through faith alone; a truly saved person may show little outward change.
infallibility: The Bible is fully trustworthy for faith and salvation, even if its human authors reflect their era's science or history.
lordship salvation: Genuine saving faith necessarily produces obedience and a changed life — Jesus must be Lord, not just Savior.
memorialist: Baptism and communion are symbols — they remember and proclaim grace but don't deliver it.
monergism: Salvation is God's work alone — he chooses, saves, and keeps sinners without needing their cooperation.
normative principle: Churches may do anything in worship that the Bible doesn't forbid — creativity is welcome.
paedobaptism: The infant children of Christian parents are baptized as members of the covenant community.
premillennial: Jesus will return before a literal thousand-year reign of peace on earth.
presbyterian-episcopal: Churches are led by elders or bishops and connected under regional authority.
progressive only: Growth in holiness is gradual and incomplete — the fight against sin lasts until death.
regulative principle: Churches should only do in worship what the Bible commands — if Scripture doesn't order it, don't do it.
sacramental: God truly meets us through baptism and communion, feeding us spiritually by faith.
strict inerrancy: The Bible is completely free from error in everything it affirms — history and science included.
synergism: Salvation involves genuine human cooperation — God offers grace, and each person must freely respond.
